texts.orig: When r = 1 , M (1 , L, c 2 ) is isomorphic to S [ c 2 ] , the Hilbert scheme of 0 -dimensional closed subschemes in S of length c 2 . Fogarty showed that S [ n ] ( n ∈ Z ≥ 0 ) is a smooth projective variety of dimension 2 n [Fog68] and computed its Picard group [Fog73]. The Betti numbers of S [ n ] were completely determined by Göttsche [G ¨ 90]. When r ≥ 2 , M ( r, L, c 2 ) can be reducible or non-reduced. But starting from Donaldson's generic smoothness result [Don90], the study of M ( r, L, c 2 ) has revealed that M ( r, L, c 2 ) has better geometric properties as we fix r ≥ 2 , L , and let c 2 increase. For example, when c 2 is large enough, Gieseker-Li [GL94] [GL96] and O'Grady [O'G96] showed that M ( r, L, c 2 ) is irreducible, normal, and generically smooth of expected dimension. Some asymptotic phenomena also occur in the Picard group and Betti numbers of M ( r, L, c 2 ) ( r ≥ 2 ) [Qin92][Li96][Li97][CW22].

texts.orig: Sheaves on S of rank zero are supported on points or curves. In this paper, we focus on those pure sheaves supported on curves, which are called one-dimensional sheaves. In contrast to the positive rank case, there are few general results for the moduli space of one-dimensional sheaves. An essential difficulty is that the supports of one-dimensional sheaves can be singular, even non-reduced. To distinguish this case, we use the following notation. Given a nonzero effective divisor β on S and an integer χ , denote by M β,χ the moduli space parametrizing polystable one-dimensional sheaves F on S , with determinant det( F ) ∼ = O S ( β ) and Euler characteristic χ ( F ) = χ . We will make the following assumption on β , unless otherwise stated.
